clue.text: Concert-goers' walk

parts.note: the Proms in London are concerts where standing ticket-holders stroll in the arena, and the word also means a seaside walkway

explanation.surface: A path or stroll favoured by people heading to a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer concert series whose name is short for this word; it also means a seafront walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a leisurely seaside walkway and the concerts named the Proms, so it is a walk linked to concert audiences.

clue.text: Piece on board that is for a beginner

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece, which stands on the board
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A chess piece suited to someone just learning the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or novice, especially a first-year recruit, is called by this informal word.

clue.text: Importance for a very short time

definitions.meaning: weight or significance, as in a matter of great consequence
an instant, as in wait a second

explanation.surface: Something matters only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means significance (of great consequence) and also an instant of time.

clue.text: A try-on perplexed a public official

indicators.note: perplexed means confused or tangled, so the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky attempt baffles an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perplexed' scrambles the six letters of A TRY-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An official authorised to witness and certify documents, a legal officer serving the public.

clue.text: Go flat out

parts.note: going flat out is trying as hard as one can, with flat hinting at level

explanation.surface: Run at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' teases toward the idea of level ground, which is in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means try as hard as possible, the same as giving maximum effort.

clue.text: Language of Peterson, a revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Peterson speaks the tongue of a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges PETERSON plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial international tongue devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Improvement now that the gambler gets some money back

definitions.meaning: an upturn or turn for the good

definitions.text: now that the gambler gets some money back
definitions.meaning: money returned is change, given to a gambler, who is a bettor, which sounds like better

explanation.surface: Things look up once the punter is paid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: change (money back) for the bettor (a gambler), pronounced the same as the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an improvement, and comically describes coins handed back to a punter.

clue.text: Care to feel inside the cartridgecase?

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece goes within the letters of the word care

parts.note: to feel something is to touch it

explanation.surface: Handle the casing of a cartridge gently.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'cartridge case' together. The word is an old paper cartridge case, and also an oval frame round Egyptian royal names.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a paper case holding a gun's powder charge, hence a casing for ammunition.

clue.text: A form of maths could leave one breathless

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so the letters are put into a different shape

explanation.surface: A maths lesson so hard it takes one's breath away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges MATHS to STHMA after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A respiratory condition causing wheezing and shortness of breath, so it can leave a sufferer gasping.

clue.text: Shape of a number of aircraft perhaps

definitions.meaning: planes flying in a set pattern together, as at an air display

explanation.surface: The outline made by a group of planes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a structure or arrangement, and also a group of planes flying in a set pattern.

clue.text: Money returned for an apple

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, slang for money

explanation.surface: Getting cash back in exchange for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note. The answer is also a variety of dessert apple (also spelt reinette), besides the curdling agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rennet is an old variety of eating apple, the reinette.

clue.text: Used when an evening meal is prepared

definitions.text: Used when an evening meal is prepared

parts.words: Used when an evening meal is prepared
parts.note: describes the matching plates and dishes brought out for the evening meal, with prepared hinting at set

explanation.surface: Something brought out when supper is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' also suggests set, as in setting the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching collection of plates and dishes put out for the main evening meal.

clue.text: Somehow get a gold finish on the cake

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A cake given a gilded top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges GET A to GATE; 'finish' says AU comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered French-style dessert, a type of sponge with cream.

clue.text: See 7 down
Exaggerated about being in the red

definitions.meaning: having spent more than is in one's bank account

explanation.surface: Someone overstating how deeply in debt they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means overdone in description and also having a negative bank balance.

clue.text: Report on a new role in an Indian city

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, a bang

indicators.note: new suggests making something fresh, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: News of someone taking on a fresh job in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROLE to LORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called Bengaluru, a major city in southern India, capital of Karnataka.

clue.text: A small weight on the vestment

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound, a modest unit of weight

explanation.surface: A slight load placed on a priest's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A long white linen robe worn by clergy at the Eucharist.

clue.text: Alternative, we hear, to reverential wonder

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Another option leading to wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech, without a sounded R, OR and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelming wonder mixed with respect or fear.

clue.text: Complain endlessly about an insect

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to beef is slang for to complain

explanation.surface: Grumbling non-stop about a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying honey-making creature of the order Hymenoptera.

clue.text: Like sugary things

parts.note: like is a verb here, meaning enjoy confectionery

explanation.surface: Being fond of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a preposition but is the verb to like.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having a strong fondness for confectionery and desserts.

clue.text: One girl in seven

indicators.note: in shows that the answer is found within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: One girl among seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, that of the first woman in Genesis.

clue.text: Gold in yellowish-grey, say, or blue-flowered plant

indicators.note: in tells us that one piece is placed within the other
say signals that a word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: beige is a pale yellowish-grey colour
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Gold set in a greyish colour, or a plant with blue blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives BAGE, a spelling that sounds like BEIGE; 'in' puts OR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb with star-shaped blue blossoms, used in salads and drinks.

clue.text: Former tree doctor in Devon

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A one-time tree surgeon in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges TREE to ETER. Devon is a county in south-west England; the answer is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city that is the county town of Devon, a place found in that county.

clue.text: One French officer, nearly 50, to unwind

parts.note: un is French for one
CO is short for commanding officer
IL is 49 in Roman numerals, just short of fifty

explanation.surface: A French officer close to fifty needs to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly 50' is a numeral trick: L is 50, and IL (one before fifty) is 49.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten out something wound in a spiral, as a rope or spring.

clue.text: Where one has to go, given time

definitions.text: Where one has to go, given time

parts.words: Where one has to go, given time
parts.note: to be given time is to be sentenced, and a convict must then go to jail

explanation.surface: A place one must visit when there is a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given time' reads as having a free moment, but means being sentenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail where convicts serve their sentences.

clue.text: I left an Egyptian city for a girl

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: Alexandria is the Mediterranean port city in Egypt

explanation.surface: Someone quitting Egypt for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction but means gone away.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as borne by Queen Alexandra.

clue.text: Reptile in furrow returned, let loose

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow

indicators.note: loose means set free, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A reptile in a groove is set free again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes RUT into TUR; 'loose' rearranges LET to TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelled marine reptile of the order Testudines.

clue.text: Shut up family in the top flat

parts.note: pent means confined, as in pent-up
a house is a family dynasty, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Locking up the family in the top-floor apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury apartment on the highest floor of a building.

clue.text: King Lear

definitions.meaning: a name borne by several English monarchs, such as the Confessor
the first name of the Victorian nonsense poet Lear

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Shakespeare's play; instead it names English kings and the limerick writer Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: A forename of eight English kings and of the poet who wrote The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Begin with fish? That's surprising

parts.note: to begin is to start
ling is a long cod-like fish

explanation.surface: Opening a meal with fish is unexpected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing gives a jolt or shock.
